PhD in Civil Engineering
The PhD in Civil Engineering at Lehigh University’s P.C. Rossin College of Engineering and Applied Science is a research doctorate in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, built around some of the largest structural testing and simulation facilities in North America.

Overview
What the PhD in Civil Engineering is
Graduate students in Civil Engineering conduct experiments across a breathtaking range of scales, using electrokinetics, nanoparticles, sensor and communications technology, and advanced physics and mechanics while overseeing some of the world’s largest and most advanced structural testing and simulation facilities.
The ATLSS (Advanced Technology for Large Structural Systems) Research Center houses the largest three-dimensional dynamic testing machines in North America, along with specialized earthquake-resistant testing facilities for real-time dynamic testing.
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering maintains the authoritative program detail — see the department page.
Research
Research areas
Doctoral research in the PhD in Civil Engineering spans 7 areas published by the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering.
Earthquake engineering
Multi-hazard mitigation
Fiber reinforced composites
Fatigue and fracture
Smart structures development
Shipbuilding
Infrastructure reliability, maintenance, and life-cycle performance
Research facilities
ATLSS Research Center
Advanced Technology for Large Structural Systems — home to the largest three-dimensional dynamic testing machines in North America, with specialized earthquake-resistant facilities for real-time dynamic testing.
Real Time Multi-Directional (RTMD) National Facility
NSF Network for Earthquake Engineering Simulation.
Degree requirements
What the doctorate requires
Minimum 72 credits from the bachelor’s; 42 beyond a Lehigh CEE master’s; 48 with a master’s from another institution. Lehigh publishes the following complete set of requirements.
Credit hours
A minimum of 72 credits for students entering with a bachelor’s degree; a minimum of 42 credits beyond a master’s degree earned in the same department; a minimum of 48 credits for a master’s degree from another institution.
Coursework
The doctoral programs do not set a minimum course requirement, but most doctoral students pursue 20 to 30 credits of coursework beyond the master’s degree.
Qualifying examination
Students planning to become candidates for the PhD take a qualifying examination.
Dissertation and defense
A dissertation and defense presenting the results of original research.
Funding
Financial support
All PhDs at the Rossin College are 100% fully-funded, however, funding sources may vary by department. Funding covers PhD tuition and a stipend.
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering does not publish program-specific stipend or assistantship figures; ask the graduate contact below what funding looks like for this program.
PhD applicants wishing to be considered for financial assistance should submit a complete application no later than December 15 for a fall semester start.
Named opportunities open to Rossin College doctoral students include the Rossin Research Scholars program, Pasteur PhD Partners (P3), and the SEED-EF NSF National Research Traineeship — see special opportunities for Lehigh PhD students.
Financial aid for Lehigh’s graduate programs consists mainly of fixed-rate federal student loans through the Office of Financial Aid.
Loan eligibility requires enrollment at least half-time — six credits during the academic year, three credits in summer.
Emergency loans and grants are available through the Graduate Life Office.
Rossin College graduate funding support »
Admissions
How to apply
Applications for admission — all semesters, all levels — are completed online. Applications open September 1; PhD applications for fall admission are due December 15 for financial aid consideration.
Application open dates and deadlines are determined by individual departments. Contact the department concerning relevant deadlines and available start terms.
What to submit
Completed online application
Official transcripts (with English translation for international applicants)
Statement of purpose / essay
Letters of recommendation (typically three)
Résumé or CV
Application fee of $50 USD
The GRE is not required or considered for any Rossin College graduate program.
English proficiency minimums
Minimum English proficiency scores for international applicants to Rossin College graduate programs.
Test
Minimum score
TOEFL iBT
Overall 81 (old scale) / 4 (new scale); Speaking 22/4, Writing 20/4, Reading 20/4, Listening 16/4
IELTS
Overall 6.5; Speaking 6.5, Writing 6, Reading 6.5, Listening 6
Duolingo English Test
Overall 125; Speaking 125, Writing 120, Reading 125, Listening 110
Cambridge
Overall 176; Speaking 176, Writing 169, Reading 176, Listening 169
Pearson (PTE)
Overall 68, with 53 or higher on each band
Scores expire two years from the test date. MyBestScore and One Skill Retake formats are not accepted. Waivers are available for applicants who are citizens or permanent residents of an English-speaking country, earned a U.S. degree with two or more years of in-person study, earned a degree taught in English in an English-speaking country, or studied or worked full-time in an English-speaking country for two or more years within the last five.

Questions
Frequently asked questions
Which department at Lehigh offers the PhD in Civil Engineering?
The PhD in Civil Engineering is offered by Lehigh University’s Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, within the P.C. Rossin College of Engineering and Applied Science. Full program detail, faculty and current requirements are maintained on the department’s own page: https://engineering.lehigh.edu/cee/graduate/civil-engineering-ms-phd
How many credits does the PhD in Civil Engineering require?
Minimum 72 credits from the bachelor’s; 42 beyond a Lehigh CEE master’s; 48 with a master’s from another institution.
Do I need a master’s degree to apply to the PhD in Civil Engineering?
No. Students enter the program with either a bachelor’s or a master’s degree, and the credit requirement differs accordingly: minimum 72 credits from the bachelor’s; 42 beyond a Lehigh CEE master’s; 48 with a master’s from another institution.
Is the GRE required for the PhD in Civil Engineering?
No. The GRE is not required or considered for any P.C. Rossin College of Engineering and Applied Science graduate program. Scores may be submitted but may not be reviewed.
What is the application deadline for the PhD in Civil Engineering?
PhD applications for fall admission are due December 15 for financial aid consideration. Applications open September 1. Application open dates and deadlines are determined by individual departments. Contact the department concerning relevant deadlines and available start terms.
How much is the application fee?
The application fee is $50 USD. Applications for admission at all levels are completed online through Lehigh’s graduate application portal.
Is the PhD in Civil Engineering funded?
All PhDs at the Rossin College are 100% fully-funded, however, funding sources may vary by department.
What research areas can I work in as a PhD in Civil Engineering student?
Research areas published by the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering: Earthquake engineering; Multi-hazard mitigation; Fiber reinforced composites; Fatigue and fracture; Smart structures development; Shipbuilding; Infrastructure reliability, maintenance, and life-cycle performance.
What is the qualifying examination for the PhD in Civil Engineering?
Students planning to become candidates for the PhD take a qualifying examination.
What English proficiency scores are required?
International applicants must meet Lehigh’s minimum scores: TOEFL iBT overall 81 (old scale) or 4 (new scale); IELTS overall 6.5; Duolingo English Test overall 125; Cambridge overall 176; or Pearson (PTE) overall 68. Scores expire two years from the test date. Waivers are available in defined circumstances.
Where is the PhD in Civil Engineering based?
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering is located in Fritz Engineering Laboratory, 13 East Packer Avenue, Bethlehem, PA 18015-3176, on Lehigh University’s campus in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania.
Who do I contact about the PhD in Civil Engineering?
Julie DeMotte, jud200@lehigh.edu is the graduate contact for the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering. The department can be reached at incee@lehigh.edu or (610) 758-3530. General Rossin College graduate enquiries go to engineering@lehigh.edu.
